passage: Note, Thursday. Nikita came to see me during the free period, straight-backed and a little pale. In the class group chat two friends had asked her to send a private photo taken at the sleepover "for the album". Nikita told them, "I'm not comfortable with that, please don't ask again." One friend said fine, and the other kept sending sad faces and "come on, don't be boring". Nikita said she felt guilty for hurting someone but still did not want to share it. I told her that saying no was her right and that a real friend accepts it. I asked her to keep the messages, and I spoke to the year coordinator with her permission. Gautam, class teacher.

qa.q: When did Nikita come to see her teacher?
qa.a: She came on Thursday, during the free period.

qa.q: What was Nikita feeling after she refused the photo request?
qa.a: She felt guilty about hurting one friend, yet she still wanted to keep her decision. Her pale face and straight back suggest she was also nervous.

qa.q: What could Nikita do if the second friend keeps pressing her?
qa.a: She could keep the messages, keep saying no, and tell a trusted adult again, as she already did.

qa.q: How might the friend who accepted the refusal see Nikita?
qa.a: That friend might respect Nikita more, seeing that Nikita can say no and still stay friendly.

grounding: A teenager sets a limit with a photo request, and an adult confirms refusal as a right and pressure as a warning sign.

passage:
Friday, late. Gautam's diary.

Today on the school trip Nikita said she wanted to post the picture of me asleep on the bus, the one with my mouth open. I said, "I'd rather not have that one posted." She laughed and said everyone would love it. My ears got hot. I said it again, slower: "I'm not okay with it. Please delete it."

She went quiet, then said, "Okay, sorry. I didn't think." She deleted it while I watched, and she even bought me a samosa at the rest stop.

I was scared she'd stop being my friend. She didn't. I told Papa tonight anyway, because I want him to know I said no and it worked.

qa.q: What was the picture Nikita wanted to post?
qa.a: It was the picture of Gautam asleep on the bus with an open mouth.

qa.q: Why did Gautam say it again, more slowly, the second time?
qa.a: Gautam probably felt nervous and wanted to make sure she understood the no was meant, since Gautam's ears got hot. Gautam might also have feared she would laugh it off again.

qa.q: What did Gautam do well when Nikita laughed?
qa.a: Gautam stayed calm, said no again clearly and asked for the picture to be deleted, so her joking could not turn the refusal into a joke. 🙂

qa.q: How might Nikita have felt when Gautam said it again?
qa.a: She may have felt embarrassed at first, then realised she had not thought about Gautam's feelings, and the samosa suggests she wanted to make up for it.

grounding: A teenager sets a limit about a photo in a diary, and a friend respects it.
